messages:
june: heads up — we saw a canary auto-fallback flipflop on friday evening. canary A hit a sudden quota spike, switched to variant-b, then the capacity fallback kicked in and traffic oscillated for ~30m. we need a better smoothing/guard approach for automatic fallbacks.

sam: ouch. do we have the timeline/metrics? was it error rate or queue depth that triggered the fallback?

june: main trigger was quota-exhausted errors from dedicated pool + GPU queue depth spiking. fallback policy ran because the model variant had lower headroom. logs attached to the incident thread.

anita: is the fallback policy purely reactive to error counts? we should add hysteresis — require sustained degradation over Xs before switching, and different thresholds for canaries vs full rollouts.

liam: agreed. we currently evaluate a 1-min window with 10 errors threshold. for canaries that’s too sensitive. propose: use an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) on error rate + a separate metric for token latency p95. only fallback when both exceed bounds, plus a cooldown.

marie: +1. also add a capacity-signal: GPU queue depth (pending_tokens) and headroom% from the pool. fallback must consider capacity headroom to avoid routing to an already-saturated region.

june: suggestion from SRE: add a rate-limited rollback path that only moves N% traffic per minute and requires a sustained improvement for M minutes before full rollback. prevents rapid oscillation.

sam: what about a "grace token" for canaries — allow K transient errors within T seconds without triggering fallback, and consume one grace token per error burst. replenishes slowly. reduces sensitivity to short blips.

anita: love the grace token idea. we should surface remaining tokens in console for active rollouts so PM/SE can see how close a canary is to triggering fallback. UX: per-rollout sidebar with metrics + tokens.

liam: thinking out loud — fallback decisions: consider a weighted score S = a*err_rate_EWMA + b*latency_p95_norm + c*queue_depth_norm - d*headroom_norm. fallback if S>threshold for duration D. weights differ for canary vs prod. config-able in rollout spec with safe defaults.

marie: concrete defaults proposal (canary): EWMA_window=60s, err_threshold=0.03, p95_threshold=1200ms, queue_depth_threshold=0.7, headroom_min=0.15, cooldown=300s, rollback_step=10%/min, sustain_before_full=600s. fallback requires both err_rate and either latency or queue depth.

june: +1 on defaults. we should also support "regional failover" mode: if region X is degrading but capacity exists in region Y, prefer region-level reroute instead of model variant fallback. need to check cross-region model parity and cold-start costs.

sam: right — add a capability check: before region failover, ensure model variant and quantization profile is compatible (same tokenizer/weights family). otherwise do variant fallback as last resort.

sre-bot: FYI — last 7d telemetry shows 12 rollouts where fallback happened; median oscillation length 22m; in 5 cases fallback retriggers within cooldown window.

anita: UX question: how much control do we expose to customers vs autoset? my vote: sensible defaults + an "advanced" section for teams to tweak EWMA windows, thresholds, rollback_step, grace_tokens. expose read-only telemetry unless they opt-in.

liam: implementation notes: runtime should evaluate fallback decision in the router service to have low-latency signals. maintain per-rollout state: EWMA, grace tokens, last_action_ts, cooldown_end. events logged to telemetry pipeline with tags: rollout_id, cluster, model_variant, reason_code.

june: yes, logging is critical — we need reason_code enums: ERR_RATE, LATENCY, QUEUE_DEPTH, HEADROOM, COMPATIBILITY_FAILURE, MANUAL_CANCEL. helps postmortems and ML QoS monitoring.

marie: gating: before we turn on auto-fallback for all customers, let's run a staged rollout of the policy itself. start with internal org rollouts for 2 weeks, add canary smoothing, then open to global with opt-in flag.

sam: ops question — how do we test this in staging? can we simulate quota spike & queue depth in the local runtime?

liam: we can extend the runtime test harness to inject synthetic metrics and assert router decisions. add unit tests for EWMA math + integration tests for cooldown/rollback_step behavior.

anita: console mockups: show a visual traffic-split chart with rollback arrows, grace token counter, and "what triggered fallback" tooltip. also an override button for SEs with audit log requirement.

june: action items: 1) liam + sam to draft router fallback algorithm + default weights (ETA Tue) 2) anita to mock console UX + token counter (ETA Wed) 3) marie to write opt-in rollout plan & staged gating (ETA Fri) 4) liam to add telemetry reason_code and test harness changes (ETA Tue)

deploy_bot: deploy scheduled: feature/auto-fallback-prototype -> staging at 2026-03-23T02:00Z (dry-run mode).

june: thanks everyone. let's avoid tight thresholds that cause oscillation. follow-ups in this thread once we have the draft algorithm. :thumbsup:
